title: A negative feedback loop
caption: A receptor detects a change in a controlled variable, a coordinator processes the information and an effector makes a response that reverses the change, returning the variable towards its set point. Rising blood glucose triggering insulin release is an example; positive feedback, which amplifies a change, is rarer.
alt: Five boxes in order: a change in the variable, the receptor, the coordinator, the effector and the restored set point.
description: Change: a controlled variable moves away from its set point.
Coordinator: such as the brain, processes the information.
Effector: carries out a response, such as a gland or muscle.
Set point restored: the response reverses the change.
Example: blood glucose rises, the pancreas releases insulin, and glucose falls back to the set point.
